name: MD2 pineapple smallholding on drained peat
headline: Pineapple thrives on acid peat, but every drained metre of peat sinks, emits carbon and can burn.
story: A 4 ha smallholding near Pekan Nanas growing MD2 pineapple for export on deep, drained peat, replanted every two years after a ratoon crop. Pineapple tolerates the extreme acidity, but drainage lowers the water table, so the peat subsides 2-5 cm a year, releases CO2, and becomes a fire risk in dry spells like the 2019 El Niño haze.

soil_overrides.hydrologic_group_raw: D (high water table on drained peat)
soil_overrides.note: SoilGrids underestimates organic carbon on tropical peat at 250 m. This field is mapped as deep peat by the Johor soil survey, so the organic-soil values here replace the model estimate.

baseline_rotation.name: MD2 pineapple (plant crop + ratoon), replanted
baseline_rotation.note: Sentinel-2 shows a permanent mid-level canopy; Pekan Nanas peat is a recognised pineapple area (MPIB).

water_context.in_situ_source: Published subsidence rates for drained tropical peat (2-5 cm/yr)
water_context.note: The key water number on peat is the water table. Keeping it within 40-60 cm of the surface slows subsidence and fire risk; deeper drains speed both.

pineapple.note: MPIB-registered packers export MD2 fresh to Singapore, China and the Middle East.
